Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

cōnfirmō

cōnfirmō, cōnfirmāre, cōnfirmāvī, cōnfirmātum

verb, first conjugation; with an accusative, or an accusative and infinitive, and a dative of the person assured

assure, state as certain; bear out; encourage, give confidence, reassure

In this lexicon

  • confirm

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.16.2: Balbus mihi cōnfirmāvit tē dīvitem futūrum; Cic. Att. 16.5.2: hoc cum mihi nōn modo cōnfirmāsset sed etiam persuāsisset

  • encourage

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. App. 23.5: vōce hospitālī cōnfirmātus restitit; Cic. Fam. 6.6 (Lewis & Short): animum sapientissimī hominis

Examples

  • Balbus mihi cōnfirmāvit tē dīvitem futūrum.

    Balbus assured me you’ll be rich.Cic. Fam. 7.16.2

    In the entry for confirm

  • hoc cum mihi nōn modo cōnfirmāsset sed etiam persuāsisset

    when he had not only assured me of this but convinced me of itCic. Att. 16.5.2

    In the entry for confirm

  • abs tē postulō atque ōrō Chreme ut beneficium verbīs initum dūdum nunc rē comprobēs

    I ask and beg you, Chremes, to make good now in fact the favour you began in words a while agoTer. And. 823–824

    In the entry for confirm

  • iterum salūtat īdem ex occultō sonus. vōce hospitālī cōnfirmātus restitit, ut quisquis esset pār officium reciperet

    Again the same voice greets him from its hiding place. Encouraged by the friendly voice, he stopped, so that whoever it was should have the courtesy returned.Phaedr. App. 23.4–6
